subject: maths
title: Time: O’clock, Half Past, Days and Months
seo_title: Year 1 Time Worksheets: O’clock, Half Past, Days of the Week and Months (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Sequence events in chronological order using language [for example, before and after, next, first, today, yesterday, tomorrow, morning, afternoon and evening]; recognise and use language relating to dates, including days of the week, weeks, months and years; tell the time to the hour and half past the hour and draw the hands on a clock face to show these times.
meta_desc: Free Year 1 maths worksheets on time: o’clock and half past on clocks, morning, afternoon and evening, putting events in order, yesterday and tomorrow, days of the week and months of the year. 100 picture questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: Long hand on the 12: o’clock. Long hand on the 6: half past.
key_sub: The short hand tells the hour. At half past it is between two numbers: use the number it has gone past, so half past 3, not half past 4.
body_html:
The two hands

A clock has two hands. The short hand is the hour hand. The long hand is the minute hand. Look at the long hand first. Then look at the short hand.

  1. Long hand on the 12: it is an o’clock time.
  2. Long hand on the 6: it is half past.
  3. Short hand: it tells the hour. If it is between two numbers, use the number it has gone past.

Half past

Half past means half an hour after the o’clock time. The long hand has gone half of the way round. The short hand has moved halfway to the next number.

TimeLong handShort hand
3 o’clockon the 12on the 3
half past 3on the 6between 3 and 4
4 o’clockon the 12on the 4
Example 1

The long hand is on the 12. The short hand is on the 9. What time is it?

The long hand on the 12 means o’clock. The short hand tells the hour: 9.

Answer: 9 o’clock

Example 2

The long hand is on the 6. The short hand is between 6 and 7. What time is it?

The long hand on the 6 means half past. The short hand has gone past the 6, so the hour is 6.

Answer: half past 6

Time words and the order of events

The day goes in order: morning, afternoon, evening. Use first, next, then and last to tell things in order. Before means earlier. After means later.

WordMeans
yesterdaythe day before today
todaythis day
tomorrowthe day after today

Days and months

There are 7 days in a week: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. Saturday and Sunday are the weekend.

There are 12 months in a year: January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December.

Example 3

Today is Wednesday. What day will it be tomorrow?

Tomorrow is the day after today. Say the days: Wednesday, Thursday.

Answer: Thursday

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading half past 3 as half past 4 because the short hand is near the 4Use the number the short hand has gone past: half past 3
Mixing up the hands (reading half past 3 as 6 o’clock)Short hand = hour. Long hand on the 6 = half past
Mixing up yesterday and tomorrowYesterday is before today. Tomorrow is after today
Saying the days out of orderSay them in order every day: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday …

faq.q: What time should a Year 1 child be able to tell?
faq.a: In Year 1, children tell the time to the hour and half past the hour, like 3 o’clock and half past 3, and draw the hands on a clock. Quarter past, quarter to and 5-minute times come in Year 2.

faq.q: What does half past mean on a clock?
faq.a: Half past means half an hour after the o’clock time. At half past 3 the long hand points to the 6 and the short hand is halfway between the 3 and the 4.

faq.q: Why is the hour hand between two numbers at half past?
faq.a: The hour hand moves slowly all through the hour. At half past 3 it has gone halfway from the 3 to the 4, so the hour is still 3.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn the days of the week and months of the year?
faq.a: Say them in order every day and talk about yesterday, today and tomorrow, for example “Today is Monday, so tomorrow is Tuesday.” Point out the month on a calendar and link it to birthdays and holidays.

items.q: Which hand tells you the hour?
items.e: The short hand is the hour hand. The long hand shows the minutes.

items.q: At every o’clock time, where does the long hand point?
items.e: At 1 o’clock, 2 o’clock and every o’clock time, the long hand points straight up to the 12.

items.q: At 8 o’clock, where does the short hand point?
items.e: At 8 o’clock the short hand points right to the 8. The long hand points to the 12.

items.q: At 12 o’clock, where are the two hands?
items.e: The short hand is on the 12 for the hour. The long hand is on the 12 for o’clock. So both hands are on the 12, one on top of the other.

items.q: The long hand is on the 12. The short hand is on the 5. What time is it?
items.e: The short hand tells the hour: 5. The long hand on the 12 means o’clock. It is 5 o’clock.

items.q: The long hand is on the 12. The short hand is on the 2. What time is it?
items.e: The short hand tells the hour: 2. The long hand on the 12 means o’clock. It is 2 o’clock. (12 o’clock mixes up the hands.)

items.q: At 6 o’clock, where does the long hand point?
items.e: At 6 o’clock the long hand points to the 12. It is the short hand that points to the 6.

items.q: At every half past time, where does the long hand point?
items.e: Half past means the long hand has gone half of the way round. It points straight down to the 6.

items.q: At half past 9, where does the long hand point?
items.e: At half past, the long hand always points to the 6. The short hand is between 9 and 10.

items.q: Half past is how long after the o’clock time?
items.e: Half past 1 is half an hour after 1 o’clock. The long hand goes half of the way round.

items.q: At half past 2, where is the short hand?
items.e: The short hand moves slowly. In half an hour it goes halfway to the next number. At half past 2 it is halfway between 2 and 3.

items.q: At half past 10, where is the short hand?
items.e: At half past 10 the short hand has gone past the 10. It is halfway between 10 and 11.

items.q: Half past 4 is half an hour after …
items.e: Half past 4 comes half an hour after 4 o’clock. Then 5 o’clock comes next.

items.q: The long hand is on the 6. The short hand is between 7 and 8. What time is it?
items.e: The long hand on the 6 means half past. Use the number the short hand has gone past: 7. It is half past 7.

sets.title: Morning, afternoon, evening and the order of events

items.q: Lily eats breakfast. When is that?
items.e: Breakfast is the first meal of the day. We eat it in the morning.

items.q: The sun comes up. What part of the day is it?
items.e: The sun comes up at the start of the day. That is the morning.

items.q: Which happens in the morning?
items.e: We get up in the morning. Tea and bedtime are in the evening. Home time is in the afternoon.

items.q: School finishes for the day. What part of the day is it?
items.e: School finishes after lunch, before tea. That is the afternoon.

items.q: Charlie goes to bed. When is that?
items.e: Children go to bed at the end of the day, in the evening.

items.q: Which happens in the evening?
items.e: Tea is the meal at the end of the day. We have it in the evening.

items.q: Which part of the school day comes first?
items.e: The day goes in this order: morning, lunchtime, afternoon, evening.

items.q: Which part of the day comes straight after the afternoon?
items.e: Morning, afternoon, then evening. The evening comes straight after the afternoon.

items.q: Put these in order: evening, morning, afternoon. Which is in the middle?
items.e: The order is morning, afternoon, evening. The afternoon is in the middle.

items.q: What happens first?
items.e: Follow the arrows from the left. The first box is wake up.

items.q: We make a cake. What happens last?
items.e: Follow the arrows to the end. The last box is eat it. (Mix it is first, not last.)

items.q: What happens next, after “water it”?
items.e: Find “water it”. Follow the arrow to the next box: it grows. (Plant a seed comes before, not after.)

items.q: What happens just before “the snowman melts”?
items.e: Find “the snowman melts”. Look at the box just before it: the sun comes out.

items.q: What goes in the box with the ?
items.e: It comes after a bath and before sleep, so it is in the evening: read a story. Waking up, breakfast and school are in the morning.

items.q: What goes in the box with the ?
items.e: It comes after the morning and before the afternoon. That is lunchtime.

items.q: Kai gets up. Next he has breakfast. Then he goes to school. What does he do last?
items.e: First he gets up. Next he has breakfast. Last, he goes to school.

items.q: Poppy eats lunch. After lunch, she plays outside. What does she do first?
items.e: “After lunch, she plays” means lunch comes first. So she eats lunch first.

items.q: You put on your socks ____ your shoes.
items.e: Socks go on your feet first. Then shoes go on top. So socks go on before your shoes.

items.q: You dry your hands ____ you wash them.
items.e: First you wash your hands. Then you dry them. So you dry them after you wash them.

items.q: Tea is in the evening. Breakfast is in the morning. Which do you have first in the day?
c: they are at the same time
items.e: The morning comes before the evening. So breakfast comes first.

sets.title: Days of the week and months of the year

items.q: How many days are there in a week?
items.e: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. That is 7 days. (5 is only the school days.)

items.q: Which day comes just after Tuesday?
items.e: Say the days in order: … Tuesday, Wednesday … So Wednesday comes just after Tuesday.

items.q: Which day comes just after Monday?
items.e: Say the days in order: … Monday, Tuesday … So Tuesday comes just after Monday.

items.q: Which day comes just after Sunday?
items.e: Sunday is the last day of the week. Then a new week starts with Monday.

items.q: Which day comes just before Friday?
items.e: Say the days in order: Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. Thursday comes just before Friday. (Saturday comes after Friday.)

items.q: Which day is missing?
items.e: Tuesday comes before the gap and Thursday comes after it. The missing day is Wednesday.

items.q: Which two days are the weekend?
items.e: Most children go to school from Monday to Friday. Saturday and Sunday are the weekend.

items.q: Which day comes just before the weekend?
items.e: The weekend starts on Saturday. The day just before Saturday is Friday.

items.q: The day after today is called …
items.e: Yesterday was the day before today. Tomorrow is the day after today.

items.q: The day before today is called …
items.e: Yesterday is the day before today. Tomorrow is the day after today.

items.q: Today is Monday. What day was yesterday?
items.e: Yesterday is the day before today. The day before Monday is Sunday. (Tuesday is tomorrow.)

items.q: Today is Thursday. What day will it be tomorrow?
items.e: Tomorrow is the day after today. The day after Thursday is Friday. (Wednesday was yesterday.)

items.q: Yesterday was Friday. What day is it today?
items.e: Today is the day after yesterday. The day after Friday is Saturday.

items.q: Tomorrow will be Wednesday. What day is it today?
items.e: Today is the day before tomorrow. The day before Wednesday is Tuesday.

items.q: How many months are there in a year?
items.e: January to December. Count them: there are 12 months in a year. (7 is the days in a week.)

items.q: Which is the first month of the year?
items.e: The year starts with January. December is the last month.

items.q: Which month comes just after March?
items.e: Say the months in order: February, March, April, May. April comes just after March.

items.q: Which month comes just before June?
items.e: Say the months in order: April, May, June, July. May comes just before June.

items.q: Which month comes just after December?
items.e: December is the last month. Then a new year starts with January.

items.q: Which month is missing?
items.e: September comes before the gap and November comes after it. The missing month is October.

The long hand is on the 6, so it is half past. The short hand is halfway between 10 and 11. It has gone past the 10 but not reached the 11. It is half past 10, not half past 11.

items.q: It is 3 o’clock. What time will it be in 1 hour?
items.e: In 1 hour the short hand moves on to the next number. 3 o’clock → 4 o’clock. (2 o’clock was 1 hour ago.)

items.q: It is 9 o’clock. What time will it be in half an hour?
items.e: In half an hour the long hand goes from the 12 down to the 6. 9 o’clock → half past 9. (10 o’clock is 1 hour later.)

items.q: It is half past 4. What time will it be in half an hour?
items.e: In half an hour the long hand goes from the 6 back up to the 12. A new hour starts: 5 o’clock. (Half past 5 is 1 hour later.)

items.q: It is half past 2. What time will it be in 1 hour?
items.e: In 1 hour the hour goes up by 1 and it is still half past. Half past 2 → half past 3.

items.q: Which time is the earliest in the morning?
items.e: The order is 7 o’clock, half past 7, 8 o’clock, half past 8. The earliest is 7 o’clock.

items.q: Which time is the latest in the afternoon?
items.e: The order is half past 2, 3 o’clock, half past 3, 4 o’clock. The latest is 4 o’clock. (Half past 3 comes before 4 o’clock.)

items.q: Swimming starts at 10 o’clock. Isla gets there at half past 9. Is she early or late?
items.e: Half past 9 comes before 10 o’clock. So Isla is early.

items.q: The bus comes at half past 8. Jack gets to the bus stop at 9 o’clock. Is he early or late?
items.e: 9 o’clock comes after half past 8. So Jack is late.

items.q: A film starts at 4 o’clock. It ends at 5 o’clock. How long is the film?
items.e: From 4 o’clock to 5 o’clock the short hand moves on 1 number. That is 1 hour. (5 is the end time, not how long.)

items.q: Leo reads from 6 o’clock to half past 6. How long does he read?
items.e: From 6 o’clock to half past 6 the long hand goes from the 12 to the 6. That is half an hour.

items.q: Today is Friday. Ava’s party is tomorrow. What day is the party?
items.e: Tomorrow is the day after today. The day after Friday is Saturday. (Thursday was yesterday.)

items.q: Today is Tuesday. Freya went to the park yesterday. What day was that?
items.e: Yesterday is the day before today. The day before Tuesday is Monday. (Wednesday is tomorrow.)

items.q: Evie’s birthday is in the month just after May. Which month is it?
items.e: Say the months in order: April, May, June. June comes just after May.

items.q: Christmas Day is in December. Which month comes just before December?
items.e: Say the months in order: October, November, December. November comes just before December.
